Havoc Scenario Stepper

14 states of one Cooldown Manager row, walked left to right. Each icon carries a verdict — what Combat Assist Plus concluded about that button — and the walk names why every available button is skipped until the press.

The reading model: scan left to right and press the first button that is not ruled out. The press is not something cap draws — press, press-promoted and below render identically. Blizzard's swipe says skip this; a red badge says skip this, and why. Every cue is negative: a satisfied dependency draws nothing at all.

Rendered from specs/havoc/scenarios.md and specs/render-shelf.md. Real Blizzard icon art at the client's 56 px, real vendored sprite frames at their real frame counts, and cap's treatments composited the way the client composites them — SetVertexColor as a multiply, never a hue rotation. This is a preview of what the addon would draw, not a diagram of it.

The row, in a state

Primitives

Every primitive the shelf declares, as a live swatch — including the ones no scenario above exercises. A shelf edit always lands somewhere visible here.

The badge art, frame by frame

Kenney Board Game Icons (CC0), vendored beside the preview. White with the shape in the alpha channel — measured saturation 0.000 — which is what lets SetVertexColor's multiply take them to the one authored red at full strength. A tint: "lane" declaration on art that measured otherwise is a hard build error.

Verdicts

The closed vocabulary. A verdict says what cap concluded; the shelf says what that looks like.

Everything on this page is the declared style. The lab — Part 7, experiments drawn so they can be looked at but not adopted — is its own page, because it belongs to render-shelf.md rather than to any spec: its cells resolve against the shelf’s reference roster, so drawing it under a spec’s heading invited the reading that it said something about that spec.
